land.text: the French colonies of Senegal and the Sudanese Republic (French Sudan), joined as the Mali Federation, 'a territory with self-rule within the French Community' from 4 April 1959

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's French Fifth Republic shape for 1958-1959 holds both (Mali 5,493 of 5,493 cells, Senegal 811 of 821); the 1960 French shape holds almost none. The federation's 1959 autonomy ('Territory of France (1959-1960)' in the infobox) is a client relation of France recorded, if at all, in the French dossier.

capitals.name: Dakar
capitals.note: Federation page infobox 'Capital: Dakar'; 'the government was based in Dakar, the eventual capital of Senegal'. Coordinates are Natural Earth's.

capitals.name: Bamako
capitals.note: Mali page infobox 'Capital and largest city: Bamako'. The pages do not date the move from Dakar; it can only have followed Senegal's secession of 20 August 1960. Coordinates are Natural Earth's.

keyframe_review.note: 1,446,277 km2 for 1960: Mali plus Senegal, the two members that 'were engaged' in the federation (the lead names 'the French colonies of Senegal and the Sudanese Republic'). The pages give no area for the federation; the 1961 shape of 1,246,690 km2 differs by 199,587 km2, the Senegal part. The shape holds from 20 June to 19 August 1960; from Senegal's secession on 20 August the ledger's split event removes Senegal (Cliopatria's Senegal row starts only in 1961, so the Senegal dossier has to found in 1960).

1,246,690 km2 for 1961-2023 against the Mali infobox 'Total: 1,240,192 km2' (ratio 1.005): Mali alone after Senegal left the federation. The shape follows the modern frontier; the page records no change of the frontier. The shape's modern-country list includes Algeria (a few cells at the desert frontier), a rounding of that frontier, not a claim. The 2012-2013 loss of the north to the Azawad rebels is a ledger event, not a change of this outline.
Same outline as the 1961-2023 shape (1,246,690 km2).

ledger.note: 1960: the seat of government moves from Dakar to Bamako. The federation page puts the government in Dakar and the Mali page gives Bamako as the capital; neither dates the move, which can only follow the secession of Senegal on 20 August 1960 (page silent).

region.text: the French colonies of Senegal and the Sudanese Republic (French Sudan)

ledger.note: 20 June 1960: the Mali Federation of Senegal and the Sudanese Republic becomes independent from France. 'became independent after negotiations with France on 20 June 1960' (infobox 'Independence: 20 June 1960'); the federation had been 'founded on 4 April 1959 as a territory with self-rule within the French Community', with Dakar as its capital. Upper Volta and Dahomey never entered it.

20 August 1960: Senegal secedes. 'Senegal declared independence from the Mali Federation at a midnight session on 20 August' (infobox 'Senegal independence: 20 August 1960'); the lead has it withdrawing 'the next day' after the 19 August standoff. The federation, which lasted 'for two months', ends with the Sudanese Republic as the remainder.

22 September 1960: the Republic of Mali. 'at a meeting on 22 September the party decided to rename the country Mali and to sever ties with the French Community'; the Mali page: 'allowed the Sudanese Republic to become the independent Republic of Mali on 22 September 1960' (infobox 'Declaration of the Republic of Mali: 22 September 1960'). Same state and land as the Sudanese Republic of the federation; the colour continues.

region.text: the Agacher Strip, centred on the Beli river in northern Burkina Faso

ledger.note: 25 December 1985: Mali and Burkina Faso fight over the Agacher Strip. 'At dawn on 25 December 1985,' the war began over 'a 160-kilometre-long strip of land along the border in northern Burkina Faso' (infobox '25-30 December 1985'; a brief armed conflict in 1974 is undated on the page). The region is the researcher's reading of 'northern Burkina Faso' (the Oudalan province).

22 December 1986: the ICJ ends the Agacher dispute. 'the court issued a ruling on the matter by a five-member panel of judges on 22 December 1986'; the fighting had stopped with the ANAD-brokered ceasefire of 30 December 1985.

region.text: the western portion of the Agacher Strip

ledger.note: 22 December 1986: Mali receives the western part of the Agacher Strip. 'Mali received the more-densely populated western portion and Burkina Faso the eastern section centered on the Beli'; infobox 'Agacher Strip is divided between the claimants'. The page gives no area; the Cliopatria shape follows the modern frontier and is not changed. Checked again on 3 Nov 2026 (fx-46 R152) against https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agacher_Strip_War and the Burkina Faso-Mali border page: they give a strip 'about 160 km long' along the border 'in northern Burkina Faso', 'centered around the Beli River', split 'almost equally' with Mali getting 'the western portion', and no width, area, coordinates or town in it, so the region cannot be placed from a page. Oudalan (43 cells) is a placeholder far larger than the western half of one strip; p1980-p1989 events/0 returns the province to Burkina Faso (keeping the one cell Mali's modern shape held), so the compiled map is not affected. Left unchanged here because any smaller region would be a guess.

region.text: Azawad: the Malian regions of Timbuktu, Kidal and Gao (the page adds a part of Mopti Region)

ledger.note: March 2012: the Tuareg rebels take Kidal and Gao. 'the MNLA and Ansar Dine took control of the regional capitals of Kidal and Gao' in March 2012 and 'On 1 April, Timbuktu was captured'; the Mali page: 'In January 2012, an armed conflict broke out in northern Mali'. The page names the regions Timbuktu, Kidal and Gao, 'as well as a part of Mopti Region', 'about 60 percent of Mali's total land area'.

6 April 2012: the rebels declare Azawad independent. 'On 6 April 2012, in a statement posted to its website, the MNLA declared "irrevocably" the independence of Azawad from Mali.' The fighting for the three regional capitals is over (Timbuktu fell on 1 April); the north is then held by the rebels, the loss event follows.

region.text: Azawad: the regions of Timbuktu, Kidal and Gao

ledger.note: 6 April 2012: Azawad secedes in the north. The MNLA declared the independence of Azawad, 'comprised [of] the Malian regions of Timbuktu... Kidal, Gao, as well as a part of Mopti Region' (about 60 percent of Mali's land). Control passed from the MNLA to the Islamist groups Ansar Dine and MUJAO (Gao on 27 June, Timbuktu and Kidal the next day) and 'all remaining MNLA held towns' were overrun 'by 12 July with the fall of Ansongo'; the land stays outside the Malian state as the rebel-held north.

February 2013: Malian and French forces retake most of the north. 'On 11 January 2013, the French Armed Forces intervened at the request of the interim government' and 'A month later, Malian and French forces partially recaptured the north, though the conflict continued' (the Mali page calls Kidal 'the last remaining Islamist stronghold' and 'the last of three northern provincial capitals'; the Azawad page: 'On 14 February 2013, the MNLA renounced its claim of independence for Azawad'). Only 'partially': the page does not say which towns stayed outside government control.

wars.name: Agacher Strip War

zones.text: the Agacher Strip, a 160 km strip along the northern border of Burkina Faso

wars.outcome: Ceasefire on 30 December 1985 after five days (25-30 December); the ICJ divided the strip on 22 December 1986, Mali taking the more densely populated western portion and Burkina Faso the eastern section around the Beli.
wars.note: A brief armed conflict in 1974 is undated on the page; the OAU created a mediation commission.

wars.name: Azawad rebellion and Operation Serval

zones.text: Azawad: Timbuktu, Kidal and Gao regions

wars.outcome: The MNLA declared Azawad independent on 6 April 2012 and lost its towns to Islamist groups by 12 July 2012; French forces intervened on 11 January 2013 and with Malian forces 'partially recaptured the north' a month later; the MNLA renounced independence on 14 February 2013 and a deal with the government followed in June 2013 (Ouagadougou Agreements, 18 June 2013).
wars.note: The Mali page: 'The conflict continued' after 2013; four rebellions since independence are mentioned without dates, and the page is silent on which towns stayed outside government control. The Mali page says French operation 'Serval' began in January 2013.

certainty.note: Colonial boundaries inherited at independence. The exceptions are the Agacher Strip stretch with Burkina Faso (disputed until the ICJ ruling of 22 December 1986, soft there before 1987) and the north in 2012-2013, held by rebels. The pages give no delimitation of the Saharan frontier with Algeria.

notes: Page budget 4 of 2 (Mali Federation, Mali, Azawad, Agacher Strip War): the extra pages were used for the 2012-2013 loss of the north and the 1986 Agacher settlement, the only border events after 1960. (1) One state: Cliopatria's 'Mali Federation' row is the Mali Federation (Senegal and the Sudanese Republic) in 1960 and the Republic of Mali from 1961; the dossier keeps one state and colour, records Senegal's secession as a split and the change of name as a rename; Senegal's own Cliopatria row starts in 1961, so its dossier should found in August 1960. (2) The federation was founded on 4 April 1959 as a self-governing territory of the French Community, but the dossier starts at the independence of 20 June 1960 as the other independence dossiers of this group do; the 1959-1960 autonomy is a client relation of France for the French dossier. (3) 'azawad' is a rebel dossier written alongside this one (the rebels held the three northern regions from April 2012; the Mali page says only 'a new state, Azawad'); it holds the land from the declaration of 6 April 2012 to the renunciation of 14 February 2013, although control passed from the MNLA to Islamist groups by July 2012. The recapture of 2013 was only partial and Kidal's later history is not on the pages opened. (4) The Mali page is silent on the Agacher Strip and gives the formation of the federation as January 1959 in the text and 4 April 1959 in the infobox; the federation page gives 4 April 1959. (5) The 1961 shape's modern-country list includes Algeria (bounding box to 25.04 N), a few frontier cells; the shape is accepted at the 0.5% area difference. (6) The coups (1968, 1991, 2012, 2020, 2021) and the 2015 agreement move no border.
